summary: A1a's 20-field v1 schema REQUIRES recordedAtMs but explicitly EXCLUDES eventKind, stageIndex, observedDurationMs, and errorDetail (DD12/Alt7). A1b's Proposal constructs event objects WITH eventKind/stageIndex/observedDurationMs/errorDetail and WITHOUT recordedAtMs. Because validateEvent checks ALL 20 required fields, A1b's emitted events will FAIL validation on missing recordedAtMs and are silently dropped — the observability channel produces zero events at every boundary.
evidence: A1a schema table: 20 fields including recordedAtMs (required, number). A1a DD12/Alt7: explicitly rejects eventKind, stageIndex, observedDurationMs, errorDetail. A1b Proposal field derivations section: "stageIndex: a file-scoped counter incremented per start event", "eventKind: 'start' or 'end'", "observedDurationMs: eventObj.timing.endedAtMs - eventObj.timing.startedAtMs", "errorDetail: the error message string on outcome: 'error' or 'needs-human'". A1b does NOT populate recordedAtMs. validateEvent checks presence of every field — missing required field returns {ok: false}. --emit-event is fail-soft (exit 0 on validation failure).
claimRef: WIRING-CLAIM A1a-SCHEMA-HOME, A1b DD8 ("A1b constructs event objects conforming to A1a's StageEvent type")

subsystem: Proposal DD5 / CLI pattern import gap
summary: The Proposal claims the CLI surface follows "the established isDirectEntry/parseArgs pattern from gate-script-base.ts", but gate-script-base.ts is TypeScript. A .mjs file cannot import from a .ts file without --experimental-strip-types (which the Proposal explicitly avoids for the .mjs path). The Proposal does not explain HOW the .mjs module follows a .ts pattern — re-implementing it would create duplication, importing it would require --experimental-strip-types defeating DD5's purpose.
evidence: gate-script-base.ts exports isDirectEntry and parseArgs as TypeScript functions (lines 39, 124). Existing .mjs scripts (sweep-fixture-orphans.mjs) handle CLI independently without importing from gate-script-base.ts. The Proposal says: "following the established isDirectEntry/parseArgs pattern from gate-script-base.ts" but does not explain the import mechanism.

summary: The A1a-DISPATCH-PATTERN claim says the CLI mode follows the "established workflow-to-TypeScript dispatch pattern" of prepare-admission-check.ts, milestone-worktree.ts, composite-reconcile.ts — but ALL those existing dispatches use node --no-warnings --experimental-strip-types (for .ts files), while A1a's pattern uses node --no-warnings WITHOUT --experimental-strip-types. The omission is correct for .mjs, but the claim that it "follows" the SAME established pattern is misleading — it follows a DIFFERENT pattern for a different file type.
evidence: All existing workflow-to-script dispatches in execute-milestone.js and prepare-milestone.js use --experimental-strip-types: prepare-admission-check.ts (line 171), milestone-worktree.ts (line 399), composite-reconcile.ts (line 939), composite-preflight.ts (line 171), proposal-convergence.ts (line 117). The Proposal's CLI surface says: "node --no-warnings workflow-event-schema.mjs <mode>". The claim says this "follows the established workflow-to-TypeScript dispatch pattern".

summary: The child A1a's 20-field schema diverges from the parent DIR-124-A1's schema (which includes eventKind, stageIndex, observedDurationMs, errorDetail). The child justifies this divergence (DD12/Alt7) but does NOT include an explicit statement that it SUPERSEDES the parent's schema definition. Both task bodies coexist in the task store with different schema shapes, creating ambiguity about which is authoritative for downstream consumers.
evidence: Parent DIR-124-A1's schema table includes stageIndex (number), eventKind ("start"|"end"), observedDurationMs (number|null), errorDetail (string|null). Child A1a's schema table has 20 fields without these four, adding recordedAtMs (number). No explicit "This child supersedes the parent's schema definition" statement exists in A1a's Proposal.
claimRef: A1a-SCHEMA-HOME ("single canonical home"), parent DIR-124-A1 body still defines a schema
